subject: math.CA
name: Bolzano–Weierstrass theorem
statement: Every bounded sequence in ℝⁿ has a convergent subsequence.

subject: math.CA
name: Heine–Borel theorem
statement: A subset of ℝⁿ is compact if and only if it is closed and bounded.

subject: math.CA
name: Extreme value theorem
statement: A continuous real-valued function on a nonempty compact space attains both its maximum and its minimum.

subject: math.CA
name: Intermediate value theorem
statement: If f is continuous on [a,b], every real number between f(a) and f(b) equals f(c) for some c in [a,b].

subject: math.CA
name: Mean value theorem
statement: If f is continuous on [a,b] and differentiable on (a,b), where a < b, there is c in (a,b) such that f′(c) = (f(b)−f(a))/(b−a).

subject: math.CA
name: Taylor's theorem with Lagrange remainder
statement: If f is Cⁿ⁺¹ on an interval containing a and x, then f(x) = Σₖ₌₀ⁿ f⁽ᵏ⁾(a)(x−a)ᵏ/k! + f⁽ⁿ⁺¹⁾(ξ)(x−a)ⁿ⁺¹/(n+1)! for some ξ between a and x.

subject: math.CA
name: Fundamental theorem of calculus
statement: For continuous f on [a,b], the function F(x) = ∫ₐˣ f(t) dt is differentiable in (a,b) with F′ = f. If G is C¹ on [a,b], then ∫ₐᵇ G′(t) dt = G(b)−G(a).

subject: math.CA
name: Dominated convergence theorem
statement: If measurable functions fₖ converge almost everywhere to f and |fₖ| ≤ g for an integrable g, then f is integrable and ∫|fₖ−f| tends to zero. In particular, ∫fₖ tends to ∫f.

subject: math.CA
name: Monotone convergence theorem
statement: If 0 ≤ f₁ ≤ f₂ ≤ ⋯ are measurable and fₖ increases pointwise to f, then ∫f = limₖ ∫fₖ, allowing the value +∞.

subject: math.CA
name: Fubini's theorem
statement: For σ-finite measure spaces X and Y, an integrable function on X × Y has integrable sections almost everywhere, and its integral equals either order of iterated integration.

subject: math.CA
name: Tonelli's theorem
statement: For σ-finite measure spaces X and Y and a nonnegative measurable function f on their product, its product integral equals either iterated integral, with +∞ allowed.

subject: math.CA
name: Lebesgue differentiation theorem
statement: If f is locally integrable on ℝⁿ, then for almost every x, the average of |f(y)−f(x)| over Bᵣ(x) tends to zero as r decreases to zero.

subject: math.CA
name: Arzelà–Ascoli theorem
statement: For a compact metric space K, a subset of C(K) is relatively compact in the uniform norm if and only if it is equicontinuous and uniformly bounded.

subject: math.CA
name: Weierstrass approximation theorem
statement: Every continuous real-valued function on a closed bounded interval can be approximated uniformly by real polynomials.

subject: math.CA
name: Picard–Lindelöf theorem
statement: If f(t,x) is continuous near (t₀,x₀) and locally Lipschitz in x there, uniformly for nearby t, the initial-value problem x′ = f(t,x), x(t₀) = x₀ has a unique local C¹ solution.

subject: math.CA
name: Peano existence theorem
statement: If f(t,x) is continuous in a neighborhood of (t₀,x₀) in ℝ × ℝⁿ, the initial-value problem x′ = f(t,x), x(t₀) = x₀ has at least one local C¹ solution.

subject: math.CA
name: Grönwall's inequality
statement: If u and b are nonnegative continuous functions on [a,T] and u(t) ≤ A + ∫ₐᵗ b(s)u(s) ds for A ≥ 0, then u(t) ≤ A exp(∫ₐᵗ b(s) ds).

subject: math.CA
name: Sturm comparison theorem
statement: Let q₁ and q₂ be continuous on [a,b] with q₂ > q₁. If a and b are consecutive zeros of a nonzero solution of y″ + q₁y = 0, every nonzero solution of z″ + q₂z = 0 has a zero in (a,b).

subject: math.CA
name: Poincaré–Bendixson theorem
statement: For a C¹ autonomous vector field on an open subset of ℝ², suppose a forward trajectory stays in a compact subset of that open set. If its ω-limit set contains no equilibrium, that ω-limit set is a periodic orbit.

subject: math.CA
name: Fourier inversion theorem
statement: If f is in L¹(ℝⁿ) and its Fourier transform f̂(ξ) = ∫ f(x)e⁻²πⁱˣ·ξ dx is also in L¹, then f(x) = ∫ f̂(ξ)e²πⁱˣ·ξ dξ almost everywhere. The identity also holds at every point where f is continuous.
